rows.jp: 耳元で怒鳴られて、我に返る。
rows.en: The shout in my ear snapped me back to myself.

ghs.en: Yelled at right in the ears, I come to my senses.
ghs.assessment: 耳元 means right by one ear or at the narrator's ear. 'Right in the ears' uses an unnatural plural and omits the acting subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She shouts right into my ear, bringing me back to myself.'

highlights.text: Yelled at right in the ears, I come to my senses.

rows.jp: 「は、はい？」

rows.en: “You were spacing out. Ignoring me. I’m hurt.”

ghs.en: Touko: "All spacing out. Ignoring me. That hurts!"
ghs.assessment: The source uses three clipped but complete accusations: he was spacing out, ignoring her, and hurt her. 'All spacing out' is not grammatical, and 'That hurts' changes the completed hurt into a present general effect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You were spacing out. Ignoring me. It hurt.'

highlights.text: Touko: "All spacing out. Ignoring me. That hurts!"

ghs.remedy: Use right or privilege in natural dialogue.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't I even have the privilege of spacing out now?"

ghs.assessment: これこれ is the narrator's excited approving or demonstrative cry in response to the referenced bit. 'Helpy help' invents a plea for rescue and reverses the utterance's function.
ghs.remedy: Use a context-consistent cry such as 'That's it!'

ghs.assessment: The personal name 新川豊 should be presented in standard Hepburn as Yutaka Shinkawa in ordinary English name order. 'Shinkawa Yutaka' retains Japanese order without an edition-wide reason.
ghs.remedy: Use 'of Yutaka Shinkawa, the man who was no longer here.'
